findings.title: JPMorgan Chase experiencing 'technical issue'
findings.summary_md: CNBC reported that JPMorgan Chase attributed delayed transactions on 16 November to a temporary software bug in on-premise hardware systems. A spokesperson told CNBC there was no evidence the issue was cyber-related and that it was not systemic, with other banks affected only where they were party to a Chase transaction. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET, and U.S. Bank said its own systems were not directly affected even though Zelle payments with other institutions could be delayed.

findings.title: Bank outage reports spike: JPMorgan says issues are resolved, blames internal software bug for transaction delays
findings.summary_md: Yahoo Finance reported reports of problems across JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, PNC, Citigroup, Capital One and Zelle on 16 November, citing Downdetector. JPMorgan told the outlet that a software bug in on-premise hardware caused transaction delays, that there was no evidence of a cyberattack, and that the issue was resolved Monday evening. The article noted that Downdetector reports are user submitted and do not necessarily indicate outages at the institutions themselves.

findings.title: n0n Ransomware Gang Claims Visa & JPMorgan Chase Data Breach
findings.summary_md: SecureBlink reported on 17 November that the n0n extortion gang listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase on its leak site with a 48-hour countdown to publication. Visa said the activity it was investigating began at an unnamed third-party provider in Asia Pacific, that its own systems were not involved, and that it had found no sign payment card data was affected; JPMorgan said its ongoing outage was a software bug and did not link it to the listing. The report describes n0n as financially motivated, with financial services making up 23 percent of claimed victims, and says documented intrusions used weak or reused credentials rather than vulnerability exploitation, including credential stuffing against more than 300 FortiGate SSL-VPN appliances.

findings.title: Visa confirms apparent cyberattack, hackers also claim hit on JPMorgan
findings.summary_md: TechRadar, syndicated by Yahoo, reported that n0n had added Visa and JPMorgan Chase to its leak site and threatened to publish data unless a ransom was paid within 48 hours. At the time of writing the group had not posted a sample or described the files or how it got in. Visa confirmed an incident at a third-party provider and said its own systems were unaffected and no payment card data was involved, while JPMorgan attributed the week's service disruptions to a software bug and denied a cyber-related cause.

findings.title: Hackers Leak Data on Thousands of JPMorgan Chase's Richest Customers
findings.summary_md: Newsweek reported that n0n published around 16,000 customer email addresses, phone numbers and JPMorgan Chase account IDs, apparently tied to the invitation-only Reserve card program for clients with at least $10 million in assets under management. The bank said vendors were targeted and that attackers reached marketing data that may include customer names and email addresses, with no service disruption and no connection to the earlier outage. The article also cited Cybernews on more than 6,000 affected Visa premium cardholders and a 502-kilobyte leaked file whose completeness researchers could not establish.
